Protection of Trade Secrets: The procedures and principles relating to the determination of the trade secret nature of the information obtained from the relevant addressees in the implementation of the Competition Act, and to the protection of these secrets, are regulated in Article 25 of the Act and between Articles 12 and 15 of the Communiqué No. 2010/3 on the Regulation of the Right of Access to the File and the Protection of Trade Secrets. On the other hand, with the aim of protecting the confidentiality of trade secrets, Article 239 of the Turkish Penal Code No. 5237 regulates the offense of disclosing trade secrets, banking secrets or customer secrets
Public Good/Service: Goods and services that lack the properties of 'rivalry in consumption' and 'exclusion'. If one individual's consumption of a good does not reduce others' consumption of that good, the said good is accepted as lacking the property of 'rivalry in consumption'. If one individual's consumption of a good does not exclude others from consuming that good, the said good is accepted as lacking the property of 'exclusion'. The said goods/services can be provided by the state as well as by private undertakings.
Ramsey Pricing: Ramsey pricing envisages that prices be set inversely proportional to demand elasticity, so that welfare losses can be brought down to the lowest level. In the case where there are demands of different elasticity (sensitivity) for the same product, on the other hand, Ramsey pricing envisages that this product be offered to different consumer groups at different prices according to consumers' sensitivity to price. While a low price is applied to the consumer group whose demand is elastic (price-sensitive), to the consumer group whose demand is inelastic
Rant kollama: Economic units' trying to influence the state so that decisions are taken that will benefit them and harm others.
Rant ya da kira: The predetermined payment made in return for using land or natural resources belonging to someone else.
Rastsal olay: A set of outcomes each of which has a certain probability of realization.
Rayiç Bedel: The value of real estates that varies from year to year according to current market conditions and supply-demand balances; it is also called market value.
Re-export: The sale of purchased foreign-origin or Turkish-origin goods that have been sold abroad, to another country, in transit or directly, without being subject to the provisions of the import and export regimes, whether or not a transfer is made for the value of the goods.
Rebate Schemes/Systems: Rebate systems can emerge in very different forms under the dynamic conditions of commercial life, and vary in their structures, workings and effects. If the earning of the rebate in any rebate system is made conditional on the purchase of a single product, such rebates are accepted as 'single-product rebates'. However, if the purchase condition in the rebate system covers multiple products or markets, the said rebates are 'bundle rebates'
Reciprocity Agreement: A type of bilateral (or multilateral) agreement made among undertakings in order to provide one another favorable conditions, or to buy from and sell to one another mutually. In reciprocity agreements, an undertaking can be obliged to purchase from the undertaking that purchases from it. Thanks to this agreement, the undertaking can obtain a price reduction by making its purchases from its own customers, or can activate its idle capacity. These competitive effects that reciprocity agreements can create
Reel döviz kuru: Or in short RER: the exchange rate calculated by taking into account the difference in the general price levels between two countries.
Reel efektif döviz kuru: The effective exchange rate calculated by taking into account the inter-country relative price changes.
Reel GSYH: Or GDP in fixed prices: the national income method measuring the value of the goods and services produced in a given period at the prices of a fixed base year.
Reel iş çevrimi kuramı: The school of thought maintaining that the changes seen in real income in the short run stem from supply shocks, and advocating the state's intervention in the economy through supply-side policies.
Reel İhracat: It is expressed with the export quantity index. The export quantity index measures the change occurring in the export quantity, on the condition that prices are fixed. Export quantity indices are calculated by TUIK.
Reel İthalat: It is expressed with the import quantity index. The import quantity index measures the change occurring in the import quantity, on the condition that prices are fixed. Import quantity indices are calculated by TUIK.
Reel Kesim Güven Endeksi - RKGE: An indicator in which the answers given to the different questions of the Business Tendency Survey are evaluated together and summarized, with the aim of bringing out the general impressions of real sector representatives about the economic outlook. To access the Real Sector Confidence Index
Reeskont: Refers to the rediscounting — the exchanging for a consideration again (rediscount) — of the instruments that have already been discounted, in other words exchanged for a consideration (discount). It is an instrument used by central banks in monetary policy implementations, under the name rediscount window, by subjecting various bills to discounting (re-discount), on the condition that they determine their own conditions.
Reeskont kredisi: The credit the central bank provides to commercial banks against securities.
Reeskont oranı: The interest rate the central bank applies for its rediscount credits.
Rejection of the Transactions: The non-implementation by the relevant financial institutions of the transactions sought to be carried out at the financial institutions. These are the transactions in which the financial institutions could not carry out the identification and verification of the identity of the customer or of the person finally benefiting from the transaction, could not determine to whom the ownership and control belong in legal persons and partnerships, and could not have information about the type and purpose of the transaction being carried out
Reliance on Intermediaries and: Third Parties: The leaving, under certain conditions, by the financial institutions of the fulfillment of the measures relating to the identification and verification of the customer's and the beneficiary's identity, the determination of to whom the ownership and control belong in legal persons and partnerships, and the obtaining of information about the type and purpose of the transaction sought to be carried out, in the customer due diligence process, to intermediary institutions or other third parties. In this case, all the responsibility relating to the identification and verification of the customer's identity falls on the third party
Repo: It is generally used in cases where the liquidity tightness in the market is temporary, with the aim of increasing the banking system's liquidity for a temporary period. The central bank buys instruments with a commitment to resell them at a future date (at the price determined during the transaction) from the institutions authorized to conduct open market operations. The resale price is determined on the date the purchase transaction is made. The institution party to the transaction also undertakes to buy the instrument subject to the repo transaction at the transaction's maturity. From the central bank's perspective, the repo transaction expresses the temporary provision of liquidity to the market within the framework of open market operations, for the duration of the transaction's maturity, in return for the instruments subject to the repo.
Reserves: According to the principle contributed to the industrial economics literature by E.A.G. Robinson for the first time in 1958, as the scale of a production unit increases, savings can be achieved in the proportion of the reserve capacity set aside to meet future demand. For example, the number of beds a large hospital leaves empty for sudden needs will be less than the number of beds left empty by two small hospitals half its size.
Resesyon: The being of economic growth negative or slow for a certain period. It can also be defined as the presence of idle capacity in the economy, or the economy's growing at a rate lower than its long-run growth rate.
Restriction of Technology: The designing by the undertaking of the new technology, although it is possible to design it in another way, in a way that other undertakings cannot use, in order to give itself an advantage — in other words, creating a barrier to market entry. This situation can be unlawful if carried out by the undertaking holding a dominant position and the other conditions are also present.
Restrictions on Resale Price: In a vertical relationship, the setting by the seller of the buyer's fixed or minimum resale price is prohibited under Article 4 of the Competition Act. However, on the condition that it does not turn into fixed or minimum resale prices, it is possible for the supplier to determine the buyer's maximum resale price or to recommend a resale price to the buyer. So that the maximum or recommended resale prices notified to the buyer do not turn into minimum or fixed prices, it is necessary that the said prices be published as maximum or recommended in the published price lists
Revalüasyon: Refers to the increase in the value of the national currency against foreign currencies. For example, the rise of the value of the Turkish lira against the US dollar from 1.3 TL to 1.2 TL (the US dollar losing value) means that the TL has gained 0.1 TL in value.
Rezerv: The total of the cash in banks' vaults and their accounts at the central bank.
Rezerv Opsiyonu Katsayısı - ROK: The coefficients determining the foreign currency or gold counterpart that can be established per unit of Turkish lira reserve requirement in the Reserve Option Mechanism.
Rezerv Opsiyonu Mekanizması - ROM: A practice permitting banks and other financial institutions to establish a certain percentage of their Turkish lira reserve requirements in foreign currency and gold.
Rezerv Opsiyonu Oranı: The ratio showing what percentage of banks' Turkish lira reserve requirements can be established in foreign currency or gold in the Reserve Option Mechanism.
Rezerv Para: Refers to the assets in foreign currency and gold held in the portfolios of central banks and international financial institutions. Accordingly, for a payment instrument to carry the property of reserve currency, its value against other currencies must be stable, it must belong to a country with a large share in world trade, and it must be readily bought and sold in the foreign exchange markets.
Rezerv para birimi: The currency held as official reserves at central banks because it is widely used in international transactions.
Rezerv varlıklar: The main heading in the balance of payments showing the central bank's official foreign exchange reserves.
Rights of Complainant: The rights the complainant has within the framework of the legislation, such as the right to lodge a complaint, the right to resort to the judiciary against the Board's decisions, the right to receive the reasoned decision, the right to be informed, the right to request that its name remain confidential, and the right to attend the oral defense hearing.
Risk: The degree to which the outcome realized regarding a future event can differ from the expected outcome.
Risk havuzu: The risk-distribution method in which several insurance companies come together and share a certain risk.
Risk İştahı: The desire to buy, which increases together with the growth of positive expectations in the financial markets and decreases with negative expectations.
Risk Primi: Refers to the additional return that a risky asset or instrument provides to the investor relative to an entirely riskless asset or instrument. The risk premium of an asset or instrument can also be counted as an indicator of the compensation obtained relative to the entirely riskless investment instrument.
Risk seven: The person who, between two options with the same expected value, prefers the riskier one.
Risk-Getiri: Refers to the relationship between the return expected to be obtained from an investment made in any asset or instrument and the risk assumed with the investment made in the said asset or instrument. In principle, there is a positive relationship between the risk assumed and the expected return. Hence, particularly in the financial markets, as the risk assumed increases, the return is expected to increase, and as the risk assumed decreases, the return is expected to decrease. Risk is generally expressed by the standard deviation of the investment's past returns (historical volatility). The expected return from the investment, on the other hand, is the average of the past returns. The risk-return curve formed by the maximum returns that can be obtained in return for a certain risk is called the 'efficient frontier', and its use is particularly for comparison and benchmark purposes.
Riske Maruz Değer: The statistical method used to measure the riskiness of the financial assets in a company or an investment portfolio. The method points to the highest loss level that can occur in the value of a portfolio, within a certain confidence interval, over a predetermined period. Risk managers aim, with the VaR method, to measure and control the risk assumed.
Riske tarafsız: The person who is indifferent between two options with the same expected value.
Riskte maruz değer: Shows the greatest loss the portfolio value can suffer at a certain confidence level and maturity; VaR = z·σ·Portfolio value. For multi-day horizons the scaling factor is the square root of days (10 days = √10 times, NOT 10 times).
Riskten kaçınan: The person who, between two options with the same expected value, prefers the less risky one.
Riskten Kaçınan (Risk Averse), Risk Alan: The concepts used to express an investor's preferences in the face of risk. While a risk-averse investor settles for a low but predictable return instead of an uncertain high return in the future, a risk-loving investor tends to take high risk even though the expected returns are equal. In contrast, a risk-neutral investor is the investor who makes no choice between risk and return.
Riskten Korunma: The securing of the investor's investment against possible adverse price movements, by using the instruments in the financial markets effectively and correctly, with the aim of protection against investment risk. With the aim of reducing the risks that may be encountered to a certain value, the investor can, by taking a long position with the help of futures contracts, purchase a futures contract with the expectation that prices will rise in the future, or, by taking a short position, sell a futures contract with the expectation that prices will fall in the future.
Ruhsatı: The document given by the municipalities, provincial special administrations, organized industrial zones or the Ministry of Industry and Technology, as a result of the conditions sought in the workplaces specified in the regulation according to the activity being met. Redemption: the transaction of eliminating the debt by the debtor through payments made at once or in certain periods. Import Substitution: the domestic production of products previously imported.
Sabit faktör: Or a fixed input: the production factors whose quantity cannot be changed in a given period.
